title: Persistent Storage: PV, PVC & StorageClass
intro: Pods are ephemeral — their disk disappears when they do. PersistentVolumes and PersistentVolumeClaims are how you keep data around.

steps.prompt: List the available StorageClasses in the cluster.
steps.explanation: A StorageClass defines HOW storage gets provisioned (which disk type, which cloud provider) — you request storage by class, not by manually creating disks.
steps.why: Without a StorageClass, someone has to manually pre-create PersistentVolumes one at a time — dynamic provisioning via a class is what lets a PVC just work automatically.

steps.prompt: Check the PersistentVolumeClaims in the namespace.
steps.fake_output:
NAME      STATUS   VOLUME     CAPACITY   STORAGECLASS   AGE
db-data   Bound    pvc-8f2a   10Gi       standard       2h
steps.explanation: A PVC is a request for storage from a pod's perspective. STATUS 'Bound' means it successfully got matched to an actual volume.
steps.why: A pod references the PVC by name, not the underlying disk directly — that indirection is what lets the same pod spec work whether storage comes from AWS EBS, a local disk, or anything else.

steps.prompt: See the actual PersistentVolume backing that claim.
steps.fake_output:
NAME       CAPACITY   STATUS   CLAIM             STORAGECLASS   AGE
pvc-8f2a   10Gi       Bound    default/db-data   standard       2h
steps.explanation: The PV is the actual piece of storage; the PVC is the claim/reservation on it. Most day-to-day work only touches PVCs — PVs are usually provisioned automatically.
steps.why: You'd inspect the PV directly (instead of just the PVC) when the claim is stuck Pending — that's where you'd find out if there's simply no matching storage available.

steps.prompt: Get the full details of the 'db-data' PVC to check why it might be stuck.
steps.fake_output:
Name: db-data
Status: Bound
Volume: pvc-8f2a
Capacity: 10Gi
Access Modes: RWO
Events: <none>
steps.explanation: Events at the bottom would show scheduling/provisioning failures, same pattern as describing a Pod.
steps.why: This is the same describe-for-events pattern as pods and deployments — whatever the resource type, 'describe' is usually where the actual failure reason shows up, not 'get'.
